karen: noticed a spike of node-level evictions in eu-west last night (~01:10-01:40 UTC). kubelet logged NetworkUnavailable + node memory-pressure but host NIC stats show heavy TX drops. likely binpack compaction concentrated network egress.

jit: were these the compact-pools runs that squashed many small gpu jobs onto fewer machines? we reduced core fragmentation but maybe overloaded ENIs.

sam: saw similar in us-west earlier. collectors showed pod probe retries -> increased probe latency -> kubelet eviction. host counters: TX dropped ~600 in 10m window.

derek: can you dump a `kubectl describe node` and `ethtool -S`? curious about tx_ring/full, interrupts, and any offload errors.

karen: paste:
```
# kubelet
W0103 01:15:04 eviction_manager.go:374] eviction by condition: networkUnavailable, pods: 6
# ethtool -S ens5
tx_dropped: 612
tx_errors: 14
rx_dropped: 2
```

ops-bot: INC-2026-148 created (P2) assigned to @eng-platform. Runbook: check compactor job concurrency, NIC saturation alerts, and schedule canary.

nina: root cause hypothesis: tight topologySpread + anti-affinity forced cross-AZ spread earlier; compactor then moved many small GPU workers onto fewer instances in same AZ but on instance types with 10G NICs. Result: user-space traffic (checkpointing, telemetry, dataset downloads) now concentrated and hits NIC queue limits.

jit: mitigation proposal:
1) throttle compactor concurrency (from 10 -> 2) temporarily
2) add scheduler predicate: prefer nodes with net_capacity_gbps >= 25 for high-bandwidth GPU workloads
3) add alert: node_network_tx_drops > 100/5m -> pause compaction

sam: +1 to simulation. last global compaction caused callbacks to backoff and downstream brokers to time out. we need a staging job to reproduce probe latencies.

derek: I'll author a canary plan for tonight: per-AZ limited drains (max 1 node/az), observe `pod_probe_latency`, `node_network_tx_drops`, `kube_evictions`. rollback if probe_latency > 200ms or tx_drops > 2x baseline.

karen: drain command we'll use (respects PDBs):
```
kubectl cordon %NODE%
kubectl drain %NODE% --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=90 --timeout=6m
```
Also we should label batch/high-io pods with `net_profile=high` so scheduler can place them on beefier NICs.

nina: cost note: consolidating onto larger instances (50G NIC) ups instance cost by ~12% but reduces total active nodes by ~22% -> net GPU spend drop estimate ~15% in eu-west. But blast radius increases; need staged rollout and customer perf validation.

jit: I'll open PR for compactor concurrency flag + scheduler predicate change and add a simulation job in staging that runs workload at 2x probe rate.

sam: SRE: please hold off broad defrag until canary succeeds. If canary green, escalate to gradual per-az rollout over 48h with autoscaler damping.

derek: Canaries scheduled: eu-west-1a at 02:00 UTC, eu-west-1b at 03:00 UTC (if first green). I'll monitor and post updates here. Rollback criteria in PR.

billing: tagging for cost impact awareness — please model the 15% estimate vs increased instance-class spend.

ops-bot: Reminder: attach logs and dashboards to INC-2026-148. Postmortem template prepared.

karen: thanks all. nina to follow up with short RFC for `net_profile` labels + example scheduler scoring config. We'll reconvene after canary. :white_check_mark:
